title: Orthogonal-per-tier cells cut by two alternately opened slit families
idea: Worse: point every tier's cells the same way so adjacent bitline columns must sit a full cell length apart. Flip: alternate two sacrificial materials by tier and open X-slits and Y-slits at different times, each selectively recessing one material, so even tiers' cells run along X and odd tiers' along Y and neighboring columns interleave into each tier's vacant quadrants.
why: Packs ~1.5x more cells per footprint per tier with no extra masks beyond the second slit, so 10x is reached at ~80 tiers instead of ~120 at the same cost (fact 2).

title: Retrofit US flexible-packaging converting lines into memory-foil fabs
idea: Partner with U.S. label and flexible-packaging converters, whose vacuum web metallizers, slot-die coaters and gravure units already run at km per hour, add enclosed ISO-5 web paths plus nanoimprint and spatial-ALD modules, and sell memory foil per square metre under a tolling model.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: a converted line costs ~$20-100M versus $15B+ for a DRAM fab, uses no EUV, no Czochralski wafers (no quartz-crucible chokepoint) and little helium, and can start within ~18 months in existing U.S. plants.

title: Eliminate the flat wafer surface: arrays built on trench sidewalls
idea: Etch 50-100 um-deep parallel trenches across the wafer and build DRAM cells on both vertical walls using tilted-implant and self-aligned spacer patterning, folding several square centimetres of array area into each square centimetre of footprint.
why: Density per footprint and per wafer: each wafer behaves like several wafers of area, cutting crystal-silicon and depreciation per bit if sidewall uniformity holds.

title: Room-temperature single-electron electrometer at every vertical bitline foot
idea: Coulomb blockade: a sub-3 nm silicon island single-electron transistor, formed by self-limiting fin oxidation, sits at the base of each vertical bitline as a charge electrometer that can resolve ~10 electrons. Lateral 3D tier capacitors can then hold 0.2 fF instead of 5 fF, because the read no longer depends on charge-sharing against a large bitline capacitance.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) that blocks thin 3D tiers (fact 2); claim 20x smaller Cs, so planar tier capacitors become viable.

title: Capacitor holes extended into nano-TSVs inside the array
idea: Repurpose the capacitor lattice: in HBM core dies thinned to ~3 um, one added mask selects every 64th capacitor site for an extended etch through to the backside, turning those holes into ~30 nm nano-TSVs spread through the array instead of large TSVs in dedicated keep-out zones.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): removes most TSV keep-out area and gives thousands of vertical links per mat, a large step toward DDR5-like area per bit for HBM.

title: Helically twisted vertical bitline pairs cancel coupling noise
idea: Worse: run neighboring vertical bitlines in parallel through 100 tiers so their mutual coupling swamps a 5 fF cell signal. Flip: swap the positions of each bitline pair every N tiers through staggered intra-stack crossover vias, so aggressor coupling cancels like a twisted-pair cable.
why: Permits ~20-30% tighter vertical bitline pitch or a smaller Cs at the same sense margin (facts 1, 2).

title: Spansion MirrorBit idea for DRAM: one split pillar, two capacitors
idea: MirrorBit stored two bits at the two ends of one charge-trap cell and died with Spansion's NOR business. Split each vertical access pillar into two half-channels with independent front and back gates. Each half connects to its own capacitor, one stacked on top and one buried below, so one 4F2 footprint holds two bits.
why: Effective 2F2 per bit (fact 4) with no extra EUV layers, doubling density per litho step.

title: Micro-mat 3D array with 64-byte pages via bonded local drivers
idea: Limit: a page may not exceed 64 bytes. Cut wordlines into 512-bit segments, each driven by its own local wordline driver placed on a hybrid-bonded logic layer directly beneath that mat, so the extra drivers cost no array area.
why: Fact 8: removing 128x overfetch takes random-access energy from about 5.9 pJ per useful bit toward about 1 pJ.

title: One wordline-cut mask halves every page
idea: Add one cut mask that splits each wordline at mat center, and re-wire the existing interleaved sub-wordline drivers (even rows driven from the left, odd from the right) so each half-wordline is driven from its own side, letting the controller open half-pages independently.
why: Overfetch (fact 8): activation energy and row-hammer exposure per access halve, for a small sub-wordline-driver area cost and one mask.

title: Gen-8.5 display glass replaces 300 mm wafers for capacity memory
idea: Substitute DRAM fabs with idle LCD/OLED backplane lines: use their IGZO TFT process on 2.2x2.5 m glass to build 4-8 stacked layers of relaxed-pitch (~0.8 um) oxide-semiconductor gain-cell arrays, dice into large memory tiles with a bonded small CMOS controller, and sell as CXL far-memory modules.
why: Capital intensity and EUV (fact 4): depreciated display capex, zero EUV, new supply outside the DRAM-fab bottleneck; ~30-50 GB per layer per panel, roughly $8-15/GB at 4-8 layers, competitive at today's 4x prices for a slower ~100-300 ns tier.

title: Zinc-tin oxide channels give indium-free 64-tier BEOL DRAM
idea: Use ALD amorphous Zn-Sn-O at ~250 C as the lateral access-transistor channel of each BEOL tier, stacked 64 high over CMOS; Sn 5s orbitals carry mobility in place of In while keeping wide-gap off-current near 1e-19 A/um.
why: Keeps the oxide-semiconductor leakage advantage (fact 3) and BEOL stackability (fact 2) while removing indium supply risk, so high-tier oxide 3D DRAM can reach commodity volume.

title: Contactless e-beam test of each tier before burial
idea: IFR: 'every tier is known-good before it is buried.' Backward: after each monolithic tier, run multi-beam e-beam voltage-contrast inspection to find open or shorted cell strings, and write the defect map into a per-tier repair ROM so later tiers and the controller route around dead strings.
why: 3D yield (fact 2): 0.5% loss per tier compounds to ~40% at 100 tiers; per-tier mapping recovers most of it.

title: Wolfspeed SiC access-transistor wafer bonded onto silicon periphery
idea: Fuse a power-electronics material into memory: build the access-transistor and capacitor array on 200 mm 4H-SiC in a US wide-bandgap fab (Wolfspeed, New York), then hybrid-bond it to a US silicon CMOS periphery wafer; SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap suppresses junction and GIDL leakage by orders of magnitude.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): refresh interval from 64 ms toward seconds-hours, removing 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss; adds an existing domestic fab to memory supply.

title: Pit-viper pit organs: canary cells time refresh per mat at 125 C
idea: Pit vipers sense heat with dedicated ultra-sensitive organs; put deliberately weakened canary cells (smaller capacitor, wider access device) in every 3D mat, check them each refresh tick, and refresh a mat only when its canaries start to fail, measuring real leakage at the actual local temperature and age.
why: Grade-1 parts otherwise refresh at worst-case 125 C end-of-life rates; canary-timed refresh cuts refresh 2-4x in typical conditions while staying safe as devices age over 10 years.

title: Accelerator ion tracks etched into ultra-deep capacitor holes
idea: Accelerator users make track-etch membranes where each swift heavy ion leaves a straight damage trail that etches into an AR >1000 pore; irradiate a thick oxide or polymer mold through a registered silicon stencil with gold or bismuth ions (not xenon or krypton beams) and etch the tracks into one ultra-deep hole per cell. Several tracks per stencil opening merge to beat Poisson placement statistics.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR 200-500 gives 3-6x Cs with no plasma etch and no rare-gas ion species.

title: Born hot: bond and stress-trim stacks at their 125 C working point
idea: Thermophiles fold correctly only at their growth temperature; do final hybrid bonding and stress trimming (tuned SiN stressor films) of the 3D DRAM stack with the zero-stress point set at ~125 C, so in service the stack sits near its relaxed state instead of under sustained thermo-mechanical stress.
why: 10-yr 125 C life: minimizes the sustained stress that drives creep, cracking and contact-resistance drift, with an expected several-fold cut in stress-driven failures at temperature.

title: Zero-capacitance bitline: one bonded sense amp per vertical pillar
idea: IFR: 'the bitline has no capacitance, so any stored charge reads.' Backward: in a vertical-bitline 3D array, Cu-Cu hybrid-bond each pillar foot (or each group of 4 pillars via a local mux) at ~300-400 nm pitch to its own sense amplifier on a logic wafer, so the bitline is only the 2-3 um stack height (~0.1 fF) instead of a 1,000-cell planar line.
why: Charge wall (fact 1) and 3D blocker (fact 2): ~10x lower bitline capacitance lets a 0.3-0.5 fF lateral capacitor give today's sense signal, removing the 60-75:1 capacitor etch.

title: Long lateral capacitors storing two bits per cell
idea: Worse: hold to 1 bit/cell because 5 fF barely yields one clean sense level. Flip: exploit the fact that a 3D lateral capacitor's length is set by a cheap timed recess, make ~20 fF capacitors whose 4x signal supports 4-level (2-bit) storage, and read them with a successive-approximation charge-sharing sense amp under the array.
why: 2 bits/cell halves the tiers needed for 10x: ~60 tiers x 2 bits reaches ~10x density with half the deposition and etch depth (facts 1, 2), keeping wafer cost flat.

title: Nanotwinned copper pads enable 150 C bonding of heat-sensitive memory tiers
idea: Fuse (111)-oriented nanotwinned copper, electroplated from US-mined copper on US-built plating tools, into hybrid-bond pads; its fast surface diffusion forms Cu-Cu bonds at ~150 C, so finished AFE-capacitor or thin-film-transistor memory tiers can be stacked repeatedly without retention-damaging 300-400 C anneals.
why: 3D tier count (fact 2): cumulative thermal budget no longer caps bonded stacks; enables 8-16 bonded memory wafers per stack with domestic inputs.

title: Fe/MgO/Fe junctions pinned by FeMn: chokepoint-free MRAM cells
idea: Inverts 'STT-MRAM needs Co, Ta, W, Ru and Pt.' Build stacked MTJs as TiN seed / FeMn antiferromagnet pin / Fe / MgO / Fe free layer / TiN cap, reviving the original high-TMR Fe/MgO/Fe system in place of CoFeB, Ta, W and Ru synthetic antiferromagnets.
why: Scarce resources: removes chokepoint metals from a ~10-30 ns, high-endurance cell and may lower stack cost.

title: Uncut wafer-scale DRAM bonded onto wafer-scale compute
idea: Po: memory has no die edges. Keep the 300 mm DRAM wafer whole, stitch reticles with redundant cross-reticle wiring, map bad blocks at test, and bond it wafer-to-wafer onto a wafer-scale accelerator so every compute tile has its own DRAM directly above.
why: Data movement (fact 5) <0.3 pJ/bit vertically; no dicing, packaging or HBM TSV tax (fact 6); harvests every good block instead of scrapping dies.

title: Micro-MLCC: nanolaminate multilayer capacitor inside each lateral 3D cell
idea: Scale the 1000-layer multilayer ceramic capacitor, a mm-size component, down to a 50-nm lateral cell: ALD a blanket nanolaminate of 8 electrode/high-k pairs inside each tier's capacitor cavity, then connect odd and even electrodes at opposite ends by selective recess etch. Eight plates in parallel give ~8x capacitance per footprint.
why: Capacitor charge wall in lateral 3D cells (facts 1, 2): reaches 5 fF in a capacitor ~8x shorter, which shrinks the lateral cell pitch and the footprint of the stack.

title: PCB-shop vacuum-free metallization for TSVs and through-tier vias
idea: Circuit-board shops metallize millions of vias with no vacuum; replace argon-sputtered Ta/Cu seed in TSVs and through-array vias with an electroless Ni-B barrier and an electroless copper seed grafted on a silane monolayer, then fill by bottom-up superconformal plating. The whole via flow runs at atmospheric pressure on wet benches.
why: HBM TSV cost (fact 6) and argon PVD removed; wet tools ~5x cheaper, and conformal seeds allow 20:1+ TSVs, shrinking TSV diameter and keep-out ~2x.

title: Copper-catalyzed MacEtch drills 100:1 holes without plasma tools
idea: Inverts 'high-aspect-ratio holes need plasma etch with W or carbon hard masks.' Use metal-assisted chemical etching with a patterned Cu catalyst in HF/H2O2 so silicon dissolves only beneath the catalyst, driving vertical holes and pillars past 100:1 at room temperature.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR 115 becomes reachable on a wet bench instead of ~$10M etch tools, using Cu, H, F and O.

title: Grounded shield planes interleaved between tiers to stop row hammer
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: deposit a ~3 nm grounded TiN or doped-Si plane in the dielectric between every pair of 3D tiers (and a buried shield line between adjacent wordlines in 2D). The shields absorb wordline coupling and collect migrating electrons from an aggressor row before they reach victim storage nodes.
why: Fact 9: decouples aggressor and victim, targeting a ~10x higher row-hammer threshold (1k -> 10k+ activations) and less mitigation bandwidth.

title: Grounded shield tiers between wordline tiers stop row hammer
idea: Worse: place aggressor wordlines nanometers from victim storage nodes with nothing in between. Flip: insert a thin grounded conductive shield plane between adjacent wordline tiers (one extra deposition per tier pair) that terminates the aggressor field and blocks trap-assisted charge migration between tiers.
why: Raises the hammer threshold from ~1k toward >50k activations (fact 9), allowing cheaper mitigation and a tighter tier pitch.

title: Magnesium sacrificial layers leave air-gap bitlines between 3D tiers
idea: Deposit thin Mg films flanking each horizontal bitline in the tier stack; after sealing, dilute acetic acid fed through slits dissolves the Mg (orders of magnitude faster than Si, SiO2 or TiN), leaving each bitline suspended in a low-k air gap.
why: Bitline capacitance falls ~40%, so the Cs/Cb ratio improves and the cell capacitor can shrink ~40% at equal sense signal, easing the charge wall (fact 1) and bitline CV2 energy (fact 10).

title: Array-only DRAM fab plus U.S. mature-node periphery foundry, hybrid-bonded
idea: Substitute the monolithic DRAM die with a two-wafer product: the DRAM fab makes an array-only wafer (cells, bitlines, WL straps, ~40% fewer masks) and an existing U.S. 28-40 nm logic fab makes a periphery-only wafer (sense amps, decoders, I/O) with sub-array-edge pads at ~1 um pitch; the two are hybrid-bonded.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): ~1.8x bits per DRAM-fab wafer, better periphery transistors, and half of each chip made in U.S. fabs that already exist.

title: Eliminate the oxide mold and HF dip-out: ashable carbon molds
idea: Form capacitor holes in an amorphous-carbon mold instead of oxide, deposit the electrode, then remove the mold with dry O2/H2 plasma ash, eliminating the HF wet dip-out and the rinse/dry steps where cylinders collapse.
why: Water: the dip-out and its rinses go away along with the oxide-mold CMP; combined with dry cleans, the capacitor module's water drops ~10x.

title: Eliminate immersion water and develop: nanoimprint for periodic layers
idea: Pattern the highly periodic array layers (active, wordline, bitline, capacitor holes) by UV nanoimprint with a master template; there is no immersion water film and no aqueous develop, and only the irregular periphery uses optical litho.
why: Water and capital: removes immersion UPW and developer rinses on array layers and avoids EUV for perfectly periodic patterns; ~5-10x lower litho water combined with dry cleans.

title: Tier address encoded in epitaxial doping replaces 3D staircase contacts
idea: Substitute the staircase (one contact landing per tier) with a vertical decoder: each tier's select transistors are grown with an in-situ doping (thus Vt) set by its binary tier address, and ten vertical gate pillars (true/complement for 5 address bits) pass through all 32 tiers, so an address code turns on the series select chain of exactly one tier, like a NAND decoder.
why: 3D DRAM tier access (fact 2): removes staircase area (~5-10% of die) and its N trim/etch cycles; per-tier doping comes free during stack growth.

title: Capacitor first, vertical transistor regrown over it, bitline on top
idea: Reverse the 4F2 vertical-channel order: etch and fill storage capacitor trenches first in bulk silicon (annealed at ~1000 C for crystalline high-k), cap them, grow silicon laterally over them by epitaxial lateral overgrowth, form the vertical-channel transistor in the regrown silicon, and put the bitline on top. The notoriously hard buried bitline of 4F2 VCT disappears.
why: Density + capacitor wall (facts 1,4): 4F2 (+33% cells/area vs 6F2) with a capacitor not limited by BEOL height and a high-temperature dielectric (k~40+).

title: Minify rank width: one-chip sub-rank access controller
idea: Build an FPGA DIMM controller that addresses each x4 DDR5 chip independently through per-chip command buffering, so a random access activates one chip's row instead of 8-16 chips' rows.
why: Overfetch: random-access activation energy (graph, KV cache) could fall about 8x on existing DIMMs. The FPGA prototype costs about $250k.

title: Molybdenum from oxychloride replaces WF6 tungsten in 3D wordlines
idea: Substitute WF6-CVD tungsten in replacement-gate wordlines, staircase contacts and buried wordlines with molybdenum deposited from MoO2Cl2 (or MoCl5) + H2, which nucleates barrier-free on Al2O3/SiO2 so the TiN glue layer is dropped and more of each 15-20 nm tier cavity is conductor.
why: Removes fluorine (WF6 releases HF that attacks high-k) and tungsten (China ~80%) at once; ~30-40% lower line resistance in narrow tiers allows longer wordlines and fewer drivers (fact 7).

title: Pitch-relaxed 30-tier DRAM in existing U.S. 28-65 nm fabs
idea: Inverts 'DRAM density comes from the smallest pitch.' Design a 3D DRAM at ~40 nm pitch (cell ~11x larger than at F=12 nm) with ~30 tiers, so density is bought with deposition and etch steps that mature U.S. logic fabs already own instead of EUV.
why: Fact 4 and U.S. manufacturability: zero EUV, depreciated tools, U.S. capacity in ~2-3 years instead of 5; cost/bit parity if tiers stay cheap.

title: Origami-folded membrane array stands planar capacitors on edge
idea: Po: memory is folded like a paper fan. Fabricate a 2D array with large, low-AR planar capacitors on a 50 nm membrane with stressed SiN/Cr bilayer hinges between cell rows; on release the membrane self-folds into a vertical accordion so each 0.1 um2 planar capacitor stands upright.
why: Charge wall and 3D blocker: ~20 fF planar capacitor in a ~0.005 um2 folded footprint, built flat with mature tools and no high-AR etch.

title: Cotton-candy spun oxide nanofibers as lateral 3D channels
idea: Electrospin aligned In2O3/IGZO precursor nanofibers onto a fast-rotating drum, as in cotton-candy and nonwoven spinning, transfer the aligned mats onto each tier below 400 C and calcine them, giving 10-20 nm lateral channels without epitaxy or Si/SiGe superlattices.
why: The lateral transistor blocks 3D DRAM (fact 2); oxide nanofiber channels with ultralow off-current beat the 13 fA tail and could remove most refresh (fact 3); placement density and alignment are the risk.

title: Inverse-opal printed electrodes multiply capacitor area twentyfold
idea: Convectively assemble 200 nm polystyrene spheres into embossed cell wells, infill electroless nickel, burn out the spheres, then coat spatial-ALD AlOx and infill a conductive-polymer counter-electrode, forming a sponge capacitor per cell.
why: Interface area per volume of an FCC inverse opal is ~2.2/r, about 2e7 per metre, so a 2 um-thick cell holds ~40x its footprint in plate area; even derated, ~20x more capacitance per um^2 with no etch (fact 1).

title: Cross-grain veneer slicing: epitaxial superlattice edges define sub-10 nm lines
idea: Plywood shows its plies when cut across the grain; grow a 400-layer Si/SiGe superlattice in a trailing-fab epi reactor, cleave and polish its edge, recess the SiGe, and use the edge as a stamp (superlattice nanowire pattern transfer) to print 8-10 nm half-pitch metal line arrays onto array wafers.
why: Line pitch is set by angstrom-level epitaxial thickness control instead of EUV (fact 4), giving wordline/bitline grids for 4F2 cross-point arrays on 90-28 nm tooling.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as a registration-free capacitor forest
idea: Inverts 'each capacitor must be etched and aligned 1:1 to its transistor.' Anodize an Al film into self-ordered nanopores (AR>100, ~25-40 nm pitch), line them with TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN by ALD, and bond the layer so each landing pad randomly contacts several pores; pad area, not alignment, sets Cs.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR>100 capacitors with no deep plasma etch and no EUV capacitor mask; only Al, O, Ti, N.

title: Pillar-as-page: activation opens one vertical column, not a row
idea: Inverts 'a page is a long horizontal row.' In a 3D array with per-pillar vertical wordlines and per-tier horizontal bitlines, one activation opens exactly one cell on each of 64 tiers, each sensed by its own tier's sense amp, so the activated page is 64 bits (one cache line) instead of 8 kb.
why: Fact 8: removes the 128x overfetch; ~5.9 pJ per useful bit could fall toward ~0.1-0.3 pJ; also confines row-hammer coupling to one pillar.

title: LTPS display lasers crystallize silicon for every 3D tier
idea: Borrowed from LTPS phone-display backplanes: each 3D tier receives low-temperature amorphous Si that is melted and recrystallized by line-beam excimer laser pulses too short to heat the tiers below, yielding large-grain lateral transistors tier by tier.
why: Silicon-class mobility (~10x IGZO drive) for monolithic 3D lateral transistors without high-temperature epi (fact 2); the laser tools already exist at Gen-6 scale.

title: Interposer-as-memory: oxide DRAM tiers in the passive interposer
idea: Under 400 C, build four oxide-channel 1T1C DRAM tiers in the BEOL of the large passive silicon interposer that already sits under the GPU and HBM, patterned with ArF at 40 nm. The interposer becomes about 100 GB of near memory directly under the compute die.
why: Facts 5 and 6: about 150 Mb per mm2 per tier on about 2500 mm2 of otherwise idle silicon, sub-pJ/bit access, no TSVs and no extra wafer.

title: IBM thermal conduction module rework for serviceable HBM packages
idea: IBM's 1980s thermal conduction modules let individual chips on a ceramic substrate be reworked several times, using spring-loaded pistons for cooling, but lost on cost. Mount HBM stacks on a glass substrate with reworkable solder joints and a spring piston per stack instead of a bonded lid. A depot can then desolder and replace one failed stack without discarding the accelerator.
why: Turns an accelerator board worth tens of thousands of dollars from scrap into a repair (fact 6 yield), recovering the good stacks and the GPU.

title: Graphene-hBN barristor access with a tunnelling-barrier off state
idea: Po: the switch is a wall electrons cannot climb. Build a vertical access device of graphene, 3-5 layers of hBN and MoS2 where the wordline tunes the graphene Fermi level and thus the barrier height to the storage node; the off state needs emission over ~1 eV plus tunnelling through hBN (<1e-21 A), and devices stack as van der Waals tiers.
why: Refresh eliminated at ~4F2 vertical footprint; risks are wafer-scale vdW growth or transfer and on-current.

title: Backside-BEOL DRAM on backside-power logic wafers
idea: Under 400 C, in the backside metal stack that backside-power-delivery logic processes already build, insert two to four oxide 1T1C tiers between power rails, directly under the logic transistors and about 1 um away.
why: Fact 5: GB-class memory at about 0.1 pJ/bit with no added wafer, package or bonding step.

title: Spinodal vertically-aligned nanocomposite pillars as EUV-free 4F2 channels
idea: Spinodal phase separation: a single co-deposited oxide nanocomposite, such as IGZO-matrix/MgO or a ZnO pillar system, self-separates into ~10 nm-pitch vertical semiconductor pillars. A coarse DUV prepattern pins the pillar lattice so the pillars register to wordlines and become vertical channel transistors.
why: Replaces EUV patterning for 4F2 vertical-channel arrays (fact 4); claim removes 3-5 EUV layers, cutting about a quarter of wafer cost.

title: Mirror-paired tiers share one bitline and one plate layer
idea: Inverts 'each tier is a complete self-contained layer.' Build tiers as mirror-image pairs flipped about a shared middle bitline film, with each pair's outer plate shared with the next pair, so two tiers need one bitline and one plate film instead of two each.
why: Fact 2: ~25-30% fewer films per tier pair, giving thinner stacks and shorter etches for the same tier count.

title: ZettaCore's molecular redox storage repurposed as a charge-multiplying capacitor coating
idea: ZettaCore stored charge in porphyrin redox molecules on silicon but died on the 400C BEOL thermal budget. Graft thermally stable inorganic redox clusters (polyoxometalates) inside each 3D DRAM capacitor. Each cluster stores several electrons at a fixed potential, adding pseudocapacitance on top of the dielectric's.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 5-10x charge per um2 lets 3D tiers use short, low-AR capacitors (fact 2).

title: Bucket-brigade analog strings storing multilevel weights in tiers
idea: Revive the 1969 Philips bucket-brigade delay line from echo pedals: vertical strings of discrete capacitor-plus-transistor stages pass analog charge packets holding 4-bit levels, read by a string-foot ADC, with ~1% level errors from charge loss tolerated by inference weights.
why: Density: 4 bits per stage on cheap tiers for AI weights and activations, ~3-4x bits per area versus binary DRAM.

title: Nanoimprint-patterned array tiers: templates replace EUV exposures
idea: Inverts 'DRAM pitch requires EUV.' Pattern the repetitive cell-field layers of each tier by nanoimprint lithography with C/H/O/Si resists and silica templates, keeping optical litho only for the irregular periphery.
why: Fact 4 and the EUV single-supplier chokepoint: removes 5-7 EUV layers from the array and cuts litho capex per wafer ~50%+.

title: Liquid-nitrogen-cooled 3D DRAM with 1 fF lateral capacitors
idea: Fuse rack-scale LN2 cooling (US air-separation plants, no imports) with a 3D lateral array designed for 77 K: leakage falls by >10^6, so 1 fF short horizontal capacitors still retain for seconds, tiers become ~5x thinner and refresh nearly disappears.
why: Facts 1-3: capacitor wall sidestepped, refresh (46 fJ/bit) near zero, and wire resistance ~5x lower at 77 K (fact 5); cryo plant cost amortized per rack.

title: Pattern first, stack later: DUV tiers bonded into 3D
idea: Reverse 3D's 'stack then pattern through all tiers': each tier is a complete relaxed-pitch (F~35 nm, DUV-only) 2D DRAM-lite layer built on its own donor wafer, tested, then ion-cut transferred onto the stack with a coarse inter-tier via; repeat 8-16 times. Density comes from tier count, not EUV pitch.
why: Litho/capital (fact 4): zero EUV layers; 16 tiers at ~1/8 the density per tier still give ~2x 2D density, using depreciated DUV fabs and known-good-tier yield control.

title: Rambus micro-threading revived as tier-granular activation in 3D DRAM
idea: Rambus micro-threading (rows split into small, independently activated pieces) was never adopted in planar DRAM because of decoder area and pin cost. In 3D DRAM, give each tier its own local wordline driver, so an activate opens one tier of one mat (~1 Kb) instead of an 8 Kb page.
why: Cuts the 128x overfetch and ~5.9 pJ per useful bit of random reads (fact 8) by ~8x, and shrinks the row-hammer blast radius (fact 9).

title: Back-contact solar layout: bitlines moved to the wafer backside
idea: Interdigitated-back-contact solar cells free the front surface by putting all metal behind; do the same for vertical-channel DRAM: after front-side capacitors are built, bond to a carrier, thin to the channel bottoms and form buried bitlines from the backside, so the front is 100% capacitor landing at true 4F2.
why: Litho-bound cell layout (fact 4): removes bitline contacts and shields that block 4F2 vertical-channel cells; claims ~33% less area per bit than 6F2 at the same F, a node of gain without extra EUV.

title: Snowshoe: wide flat multilayer-plate capacitor replaces the tall cylinder
idea: A snowshoe spreads weight wide instead of sinking deep: replace the tall cylinder with ~20 alternating TiN and ZrO2/HfO2 horizontal plates deposited as a blanket stack, patterned once per cell, with odd plates tied to a storage post and even plates to a shared plate post by sidewall-selective recess and fill (MLCC-style). Only the capacitor module changes; the die and its DDR5/HBM interface do not.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): 4-6 fF from ~0.4 um of stack height with no high-AR hole etch and no pillar-collapse yield loss.

title: One crucible wafer seeds twenty monocrystalline tiers by donor reuse
idea: Limit: at most one CZ (quartz-crucible) wafer per 20 tiers. Smart-cut transfers 60 nm single-crystal Si films from one donor onto the stack one tier at a time, with refinishing CMP between transfers. The donor is reused about 20 times before it is sliced into test wafers.
why: Resource chokepoint: Spruce Pine high-purity quartz; cuts crucible-grown Si per tier-bit about 20x while keeping crystalline access transistors.

title: Aerospace honeycomb: hex-packed cells with three 120-degree line sets
idea: Adapted from honeycomb sandwich cores: vertical-channel cells sit on a hexagonal close-packed lattice addressed by three line families at 120 degrees (wordline, bitline, plate-select), with a cell chosen by coincidence of two of them.
why: Hex packing gives ~3.5F2 vs 4F2 square and 6F2 today (fact 4), ~15% more bits per litho area, plus isotropic support that resists tall-pillar collapse.

title: Charge-coupled vertical pillar: bucket-brigade string instead of per-tier wordlines
idea: IFR: 'no tier needs its own decoder.' Backward: make each vertical pillar a 32-stage charge-coupled shift register with three clock-phase gate planes repeated up the stack; bits are clocked down to one regenerating sense amp at the pillar foot and recirculated, like a CCD image column.
why: 3D blocker and periphery (facts 2, 7): three clock planes replace 32 wordline drivers and the staircase; ~16 ns pillar latency at 2 GHz shift, and circulation doubles as refresh.

title: Sodium-calcium glass panels host display-style oxide DRAM tiers
idea: Fabricate stacked oxide-TFT 2T0C/1T1C arrays on SiN-barriered soda-lime (Na, Ca, Si, O) glass using i-line or proximity litho and sputtering, as the university prototype of a display-fab memory line where one Gen-8.5 panel (~5.5 m2) offers ~78x the area of a 300 mm wafer.
why: Attacks capital intensity (fact 4) by repurposing idle LCD fabs and cheap glass for bulk-capacity, refresh-light memory tiers built from the most abundant elements on the table.

title: Mobile-shelving sense amps: one aisle serves eight stacked mats
idea: Like compact library shelving that opens one aisle at a time, put one sense-amp stripe at the base of eight vertically bonded subarrays sharing a vertical bitline through isolation switches, so only the opened subarray connects to the amplifiers at a time.
why: Periphery ~49% (fact 7): sense-amp area amortized 8x instead of today's 2x shared-SA; claims ~25-30% smaller die.

title: Cross-laminated timber: each conductor plane serves two tiers
idea: Like CLT boards glued with alternating grain, conductor planes alternate X/Y orientation: each plane is the bitline of the tier below and, through a thin gate dielectric, the gate/wordline of the tier above, with an oxide-semiconductor cell at every crossing.
why: Halves deposition/etch layers per tier (~4 to ~2), cutting stack height and per-tier cost ~40% and pulling the 26-tier break-even (fact 2) toward ~15 tiers.

title: Aging KV cache in never-refreshed tiers, models trained to forget
idea: Po: let memory forget like a brain. Store KV-cache and activation low-order bit-slices in never-refreshed tiers and sign/high bits in protected tiers, and train models with the measured 1-to-0 decay statistics so old entries gracefully lose precision (8b toward 4b) as they age, matching how attention importance decays.
why: Refresh zero for ~half of AI working capacity; accuracy loss targeted <0.5% through decay-aware training.

title: Double-helix twin cells: complementary bit pairs in adjacent tiers
idea: DNA pairs every base with its complement so damage is detectable; store each bit as true and complement charge in two cells in vertically adjacent tiers of the same column, which share temperature, process and leakage environment, and sense them differentially against each other so 125 C leakage becomes common-mode.
why: Leakage rises ~30-100x from 25 to 125 C; twin sensing doubles signal and tracks drift for ~4-8x retention per bit, trading 2x cheap tiers for 125 C operation without 8x refresh.

title: Embargoed engineer's tungsten-free wordline: doped epitaxial gate tiers
idea: Without Chinese tungsten, the embargoed engineer grows the wordline in the same epi run as the channel. A degenerately boron-doped SiGe layer in each tier is the gate, wordlines are segmented every 512 cells and strapped to copper at each segment end.
why: Removes W replacement metal from 3D arrays (tungsten chokepoint) and also drops a CVD-W module and its fill-void yield loss.

title: TSV-free memory stacks with inductive coupling between dies
idea: Po: the stack has no wires through it. Stack thinned DRAM dies with power fed by edge wraps and move data through on-die spiral coils at ~30 um pitch that couple inductively through 5-10 dies, placing coils over array area with no keep-out zones.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): reclaims TSV area and the 20-30% yield loss from TSV processing.

title: Redox-molecule pseudocapacitor storage node on nanoporous electrode
idea: Under 400 C, a nanoporous Ru storage node (about 50x surface area) is coated at 200 C with a monolayer of thermally robust porphyrin redox molecules. Bits are stored as molecular oxidation state, so many electrons are packed per nm2 at low voltage.
why: Facts 1 and 10: about 10x charge per footprint versus dielectric capacitors at about 0.5 V reads; planar storage nodes.

title: Crystal-growing alien: epitaxial SrTiO3 capacitors on silicon tier sidewalls
idea: A species that grows its tools as single crystals would make the dielectric epitaxial. Sr-passivate the (001) sidewalls of single-crystal Si tiers and grow epitaxial SrTiO3 by MBE or ALD with no SiO2 interlayer, against a degenerately doped Si electrode.
why: Effective k of ~70-100 meets Fact 1's 'k ~70' target and makes the lateral capacitor in 3D DRAM 3-4x shorter (Fact 2).

title: Electrolytic-capacitor cells: anodize a porous niobium sponge for conformal dielectric
idea: Scale the electrolytic capacitor down to a cell: sputter a columnar, porous Nb film by glancing-angle deposition onto each 180-nm storage node, then anodize it so conformal Nb2O5 (k~40) grows inside every pore, with thickness set by voltage at ~2 nm/V. Surface area rises ~20x without any high-AR lithographic etch.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): >5 fF in a short structure from beaker anodization, avoiding tantalum and AR-75 etches.

title: Area-selective ALD replaces deposit-then-etch for tier dielectrics
idea: Substitute 'deposit everywhere, then etch' with area-selective ALD: small-molecule inhibitors (acetylacetone, aminosilanes, or alkanethiol monolayers on metal) block nucleation on a tier's metal/semiconductor faces so Al2O3/ZrO2 grows only on dielectric faces (and vice versa for Mo), self-aligning each tier's isolation and capacitor dielectric with no dielectric etch.
why: Removes fluorocarbon dielectric etches and the overlay error that blocks dense 4F² (fact 4); each self-aligned step deletes a litho+etch pair.

title: Magnify bitline to 4096 cells using current-read gain cells
idea: In a vertical-bitline 3D array, hang 4096 tiered 3T gain cells on one bitline. They are read non-destructively by current, not by charge sharing, so bitline capacitance no longer limits signal and one sense amp serves 8x more cells than in 1T1C.
why: Periphery takes 49% of the die: sense-amp and bitline-driver area per bit falls by about 8x, which could free 25-30% of die area for cells.

title: Minify the data path: each mat bonds straight down to logic
idea: Hybrid-bond every DRAM mat's local I/O directly to the logic die below at 1-2 um pitch, removing global datalines and the PHY, for a 65,536-bit-wide interface at about 250 MHz.
why: Data movement and periphery: I/O energy could fall from 3-4 pJ/bit to about 0.05-0.1 pJ/bit, and global bus area drops about 10% of the die.

title: Eliminate oxide CMP: vacuum glass reflow planarization
idea: Return to pre-CMP practice: cap each tier with a low-melting borophosphosilicate glass and reflow it under vacuum so surface tension planarizes it, with a dry etch-back to target thickness.
why: Water: dielectric CMP and post-CMP cleans recur on every tier of a 3D stack; reflow removes slurry and brush-clean water, roughly 10x per planarization step.

title: Eliminate identical tiers: hot short-bitline tiers over dense tiers
idea: Build the top 4 tiers of a 3D stack with short bitlines and fast, frequently refreshed cells and the lower tiers with long bitlines and dense cells; an on-die migration engine moves hot rows upward over vertical bitline bridges.
why: Latency vs density: near-SRAM-class latency for the hot set and maximum density for the bulk in one stack, with ~20% lower average access energy.

title: Edge-wired stacks: plated copper down die edges replaces TSVs
idea: Inverts 'vertical signals must pass through the die.' Stack thinned DRAM dies with staggered setbacks and plate or print Cu/Al traces down the stepped edges to the base die, so no TSV keep-out zones or TSV liners are needed.
why: Fact 6: removes much of HBM's TSV area tax and TSV yield loss, using Cu/Al only with no W or Ta.

title: Baker's leavened bread: dealloyed nanoporous metal capacitor electrodes
idea: Bread rises because yeast leaves holes. Sputter a 300 nm Ag-Au or Cu-Mn alloy, dealloy it in acid to a nanoporous metal with 15-30 nm ligaments, then coat it with ALD high-k and an ALD TiN top electrode.
why: ~10-20x electrode area per footprint at 0.3 um height instead of 70:1 pillars (Fact 1). A sputter tool, an acid bath and ALD fit a small team.

title: All-silicon tier superlattice isolated by doping-selective porosification
idea: Inverts '3D tiers need Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattices.' Grow alternating p+ and lightly doped Si epi layers, electrochemically convert only the p+ layers to porous Si through slits, then oxidize them into buried oxide, giving stacked single-crystal SOI tiers from Si and B alone.
why: Fact 2: crystalline 3D tiers without Ge or per-tier wafer bonding; one epi run makes dozens of tiers.

title: Heterogeneous tier recipes: fat-capacitor base, gain-cell upper tiers
idea: Inverts 'all cells in a stack are identical.' Build the bottom single-crystal tiers as long-retention capacitor cells and the upper, low-thermal-budget tiers as cheap capacitor-free short-retention gain cells used as a hot buffer, with a base-die engine that migrates rows between the two classes over the vertical bitline.
why: Facts 2-3: upper tiers need no capacitor so each costs less, lowering the break-even tier count; refresh effort concentrates on the few hot rows.

title: Ga2O3-channel tiers with planar 0.5 fF capacitors
idea: Under 400 C, ALD amorphous Ga2O3 (4.8 eV gap) access transistors leak orders of magnitude less than Si. Each tier then needs only a flat 0.5 fF MIM capacitor beside the transistor, with no pillar at all, and tiers become simple planar layers.
why: Facts 1 and 3: retention long enough for a 0.5 fF node removes the high-AR capacitor and nearly eliminates refresh energy.

title: Self-ordering anodic pore lattice sets the cell pitch litho-free
idea: Borrow anodized-aluminium battery and supercapacitor electrodes: anodize a deposited Al film over a coarse seed pattern (every 4th site) so it self-organizes into a hexagonal pore lattice at ~30 nm pitch and AR >100, then use the same pores as templates for both vertical-channel access transistors and capacitors in one self-aligned lattice.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4) and capacitor AR (fact 1): bottom-up hexagonal 4F2-equivalent array with only coarse lithography; claims elimination of 2-3 EUV layers and AR >100 at no etch cost.

title: Pacemaker nanowatt array: 8-tier vertical bitlines with local gain
idea: A pacemaker budget means tiny bitline swings; give each vertical bitline only 8 tiers of cells and a one-transistor gain stage at its base, so local bitline capacitance is ~0.1 fF and a 1 fF capacitor still develops ~450 mV. The gain stage alone drives the long global bitline.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): Cs can drop ~5x to ~1 fF, a shallow capacitor that fits lateral 3D tiers (fact 2); bitline energy down ~10x (fact 10).

title: Mo wordline surface sulfurized into its own MoS2 channel
idea: Combine wordline and channel from one element: after each 3D tier's Mo wordline and an ALD HfO2 gate dielectric (Oregon hafnium), a thin Mo film on top is sulfurized below 450 C into 2-3-layer MoS2, giving a self-aligned, atomically thin access channel per tier.
why: Facts 2-3: ~1.6-1.8 eV few-layer MoS2 cuts off-leakage below Si and a 2 nm channel keeps tiers thin; all-US supply (Climax Mo, refinery sulfur, domestic Hf) and no indium/gallium.

title: CTE-matched molybdenum TSVs dropped inside the cell array
idea: Fill TSVs with domestic molybdenum, whose ~5 ppm/K expansion nearly matches silicon, so stress keep-out zones shrink from ~10 um to <1 um and TSVs can sit inside the subarray grid (in sense-amp gaps) instead of dedicated TSV channels.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): reclaims ~5-10% die area, avoids China-dominated tungsten and Cu-pumping yield loss, and allows more channels per stack.

title: Talbot interference lithography for perfectly periodic array layers
idea: Worse: run a $200M single-source EUV scanner to print what is just a periodic grating. Flip: print the array's hole and line layers with achromatic Talbot or multi-beam immersion interference exposure, whose 'mask' is a cheap grating, and keep DUV only for aperiodic cut and periphery layers.
why: Removes most of the 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4); interference tools cost ~5-10x less and have no single-supplier chokepoint.

title: Logic-on-top stacking keeps DRAM tiers cool, with per-tier refresh
idea: Flip the HBM-style stack so the hot logic die sits against the heatsink and DRAM tiers hang below it, and embed a thermal diode in every tier that sets that tier's own refresh interval.
why: Leakage is Arrhenius (Ea ~0.6 eV), about 2x per 10 C, so running DRAM 15-20 C cooler cuts refresh rate 3-4x (fact 3), and per-tier refresh stops the whole stack refreshing at the hottest tier's rate.

title: Termite-mound chimneys: heat-pipe pillars threaded through the stack
idea: Adapted from termite-mound ventilation shafts: every 64th vertical bitline slot in a DRAM-on-logic stack becomes a Cu/diamond 'chimney' pillar tying all tiers to a top heat spreader, holding every tier within ~5 C of the coolant.
why: Retention roughly halves per ~10 C, so cooler tiers cut refresh power ~2-4x (fact 3) and allow DRAM stacked directly on hot accelerators (fact 5).

title: Correlated double sampling sense amps read 0.2 fF cells
idea: Sample the bitline before and after charge sharing onto two capacitors in a logic-process sense amp and amplify the difference, cancelling offset and 1/f noise so the required signal approaches the sqrt(kT/C) floor instead of a 6-sigma mismatch margin.
why: First principles: sqrt(kT/C) for a 30 fF bitline is ~0.37 mV, so ~3 mV suffices versus ~80-100 mV today; Cs can fall from ~5 fF to ~0.2-0.5 fF, dissolving the charge wall (fact 1) and enabling lateral capacitors in 3D (fact 2).

title: Reconstituted known-good array dies bonded wafer-to-wafer onto periphery
idea: Combine fan-out wafer reconstitution with wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding: tested good array dies are placed into a reconstituted 300 mm carrier at a US advanced-packaging center (e.g., SkyWater Florida), planarized, then bonded in one step to a periphery wafer.
why: 3D/HBM yield (fact 6): W2W throughput without compounding yield loss, since bad array dies never kill good periphery; ~15-25% more good stacks per wafer pair.

title: Minify TSV count 4x with PAM-4 and time-multiplexed vias
idea: Design TSV transceivers that send PAM-4 at 2x the symbol rate, with 2:1 time-multiplexing, so a quarter of the TSVs carry the same bandwidth. Validate on a TSV interposer MPW and license to stack makers.
why: HBM TSV tax: TSV keep-out area and drilling yield loss could fall about 4x. The test vehicle costs about $500k.

title: Magnify coil count, minify TSVs: inductive-coupled die stack
idea: Tape out a $100k 40 nm MPW chip with thousands of top-metal micro-coils as through-chip wireless links, then thin and glue-stack 8 dies with no TSVs to prove the bandwidth, energy per bit and yield gain.
why: HBM TSV tax: removes TSV area and the drilling yield loss. Proves inter-die links below 1 pJ/bit within budget.

title: Open-source hacker's memory compiler for a U.S. open-PDK fab
idea: In the Linux spirit, a 10-person team publishes an open-source generator for 3T gain-cell macros boosted with stacked metal-oxide-metal capacitors on SkyWater 130/90 nm and GF 22FDX, with layout, refresh controller and characterization.
why: ~2-3x denser than SRAM and made in a U.S. fab. Moves embedded buffers off commodity DRAM and SRAM supply, and is a U.S. manufacturability win.

title: Spalled device-layer stacking: one wafer yields twenty memory tiers
idea: IFR: 'the substrate is consumed zero times.' Backward: after front-end processing, lift off a ~10 um device layer by stressor-induced spalling (or hydrogen-implant splitting), bond it onto the growing stack, re-polish the parent wafer and repeat ~20 times.
why: Scarce resources and capital: ~20x fewer ingots (and Spruce Pine quartz crucibles) per stacked bit; wafer cost amortized over tiers.

title: Helical parking-ramp tier contacts instead of a staircase
idea: Like a spiral parking ramp reaching every level without stairs, deposit the tier stack conformally over a pre-etched helical ramp in a ring trench; after one planarization every tier surfaces at a different angular position on a flat ring, contacted by a single litho of radial vias.
why: 3D staircase cost and area (facts 2, 7): N trim-etch cycles become one ramp etch plus CMP; claims ~5x smaller contact region for 64+ tiers.

title: Magnify sharing: eight array-only wafers on one periphery wafer
idea: Bond eight array-only wafers (cells, wordlines and bitlines; about 4 masks each, no periphery) onto one CMOS periphery wafer. Nano-TSV global bitline risers and a tier-select transistor let each sense amp serve all eight tiers.
why: Periphery takes 49% of the die: periphery area per bit falls 8x, and array wafers drop most critical and periphery masks.
